pokemon.name: Charizard
pokemon.strengths: High Special Attack (109) and Speed (100). Excellent offensive coverage with Fire/Flying STAB. Solar Power in sun makes it a nuclear threat. Access to Dragon Pulse and Focus Blast for coverage.
pokemon.strategy:
Charizard excels as a special attacker with multiple viable sets:

**Solar Power Sweeper (Sun Teams):**
- Ability: Solar Power (1.5× Special Attack in sun, but loses HP)
- Moves: Fire Blast, Solar Beam, Air Slash, Focus Blast
- Item: Life Orb or Choice Specs
- Strategy: Pair with Drought setter (Torkoal, Ninetales). Devastating power but short-lived due to HP drain.

**Blaze Pivot (Balanced Teams):**
- Ability: Blaze (boosts Fire moves at low HP)
- Moves: Flamethrower, Air Slash, Roost, Will-O-Wisp
- Item: Heavy-Duty Boots (negates Stealth Rock)
- Strategy: More defensive. Roost for longevity, Will-O-Wisp cripples physical attackers.

**Mega Charizard Y (if available):**
- Sets permanent sun on entry
- Massive Special Attack boost
- Best Charizard forme for competitive play

**Key Weaknesses:**
- Always run Heavy-Duty Boots or have Rapid Spin/Defog support
- Vulnerable to priority moves (Aqua Jet, Sucker Punch)
- Relatively frail Defense (78 base)

**Best Partners:**
- Rapid Spin/Defog users: Corviknight, Great Tusk, Torkoal
- Drought setters: Torkoal, Ninetales (for Solar Power sets)
- Electric immunities: Ground-types to handle Electric attacks
- Stealth Rock setters: Pressure opponents, force switches

**The matchup behind the 4× Rock weakness:**
Charizard's Fire/Flying typing gives it a Ground immunity and useful resistances to Fire, Grass, Fighting, Bug, Steel, and Fairy, including especially strong Grass and Bug resistances. Rock is the central risk because it deals 4× damage; Water and Electric deal 2×. Stealth Rock can remove half of Charizard's health when it enters, so Heavy-Duty Boots or dependable hazard removal is normally essential. Do not evaluate a switch from the type chart alone: a resisted attack may still carry Knock Off, status, or secondary coverage that removes Charizard before it can use its offensive stats.

**Choosing an offensive plan:**
Base Charizard's 109 Special Attack and 100 Speed favor special pressure. Fire STAB becomes especially dangerous in sun, while Flying STAB covers Fighting, Grass, and Bug targets. Solar Beam can punish Water-, Ground-, and Rock-based answers in sun, and Focus Blast can target some Rock types, but both choices have conditions or accuracy costs. A balanced set may prefer Flamethrower, Air Slash, Roost, and a utility move rather than maximum immediate damage. Scout the opposing team and preserve the move that breaks Charizard's actual counter instead of revealing every coverage option early.

**Counterplay and team support:**
Keep Stealth Rock active, remove Heavy-Duty Boots, or pressure hazard removal to shorten Charizard's useful life. Faster attackers, priority, rain-boosted Water attacks, and accurate Electric moves can be more reliable than gambling on Stone Edge. Charizard wants partners that remove hazards and absorb Rock, Water, and Electric pressure; Ground types are valuable against Electric, while bulky Water or Grass partners can cover other lanes. In return, Charizard can enter on Ground attacks and threaten Grass or Steel opponents. Forms, abilities, and legal mechanics vary by game, so confirm the format before applying a moveset.

**Planning turns around weather and recovery:**
Sun changes several decisions at once: it strengthens Fire attacks, enables one-turn Solar Beam, weakens opposing Water damage, and may activate Solar Power. The same plan also accelerates recoil and chip, so calculate how many attacks Charizard can actually make after entry hazards, Life Orb, Solar Power, or resisted damage. Roost extends a game only when the opponent cannot use that turn to set hazards, boost, or bring in a hard answer. When sun is absent, avoid treating Solar Beam as dependable coverage because the charging turn can surrender momentum. A good Charizard turn either removes a key defender, forces meaningful progress, or preserves enough health for a later Ground immunity; damage without a follow-up plan is rarely worth sacrificing its limited entries.

pokemon.name: Blastoise
pokemon.strengths: Solid bulk on both sides. Access to Rapid Spin for hazard removal.
pokemon.strategy: Blastoise works best as a bulky spinner or special tank. Rain Dish + Rain teams give it passive recovery. Mega Blastoise with Mega Launcher boosts Pulse moves significantly.

pokemon.name: Venusaur
pokemon.strengths: Great bulk and Chlorophyll doubles Speed in sun. Grass/Poison gives good defensive typing.
pokemon.strategy: Venusaur shines on Sun teams with Chlorophyll. Sleep Powder + Growth makes it a dangerous sweeper. Also effective as a bulky pivot with Giga Drain recovery.

pokemon.name: Pikachu
pokemon.strengths: Light Ball doubles Attack and Special Attack. Fast but fragile.
pokemon.strategy: Pikachu is only viable with Light Ball. Volt Tackle hits hard but has recoil. In competitive, outclassed by Raichu and other Electric types, but Light Ball makes it a glass cannon.

pokemon.name: Garchomp
pokemon.strengths: Incredible Attack and Speed. Dragon/Ground STAB covers most of the metagame.
pokemon.strategy: Garchomp is one of the most dominant Pokemon in competitive play. Swords Dance + Scale Shot makes it a terrifying sweeper. Its 4× Ice weakness is the main vulnerability — always scout for Ice Beam/Ice Shard.

pokemon.name: Dragonite
pokemon.strengths: Multiscale halves damage at full HP. Extreme Speed provides priority. Versatile attacker.
pokemon.strategy:
Dragonite is most threatening when Multiscale is intact. At full HP, Multiscale reduces damage from an incoming hit, which can create a Dragon Dance opportunity against a passive target or a resisted attack. That protection ends as soon as Dragonite is chipped, so entry hazards, status, weather, and weak priority all change the matchup. Keep hazards off the field when Multiscale is central to the plan, and do not assume an apparent setup turn is safe if the opponent can break the ability before attacking again.

Dragon Dance turns Dragonite's 134 Attack and middling base 80 Speed into a potential late-game win condition. Dragon STAB supplies strong neutral pressure, Earthquake punishes Steel-, Rock-, and Electric-type targets, and Extreme Speed can finish a faster weakened opponent before it moves. However, Dragon attacks do nothing to Fairy types and Ground attacks fail against Flying types or Levitate. Reveal coverage only when it solves the opponent's remaining answer; using Outrage too early can lock Dragonite into a move that gives a Fairy a free switch.

The type chart's central warning is Ice: Dragon/Flying takes 4× damage from it. A strong Ice move, Ice Shard, or an unexpected Ice coverage attack should normally force Dragonite out unless Multiscale, a Tera type, or another game-specific effect changes the calculation. Rock, Dragon, and Fairy moves are also super effective. Steel-, Water-, or Fire-type teammates can help manage Ice pressure, while hazard removal protects Multiscale. Conversely, counter Dragonite by keeping its Ice answer healthy, denying Dragon Dance turns with phazing, Taunt, status, or immediate pressure, and checking the revealed item before committing a revenge killer. Use the team calculator to make sure a Dragonite slot does not concentrate Ice and Rock weaknesses elsewhere on the roster.

pokemon.name: Tyranitar
pokemon.strengths: Sand Stream gives Tyranitar immediate weather value alongside 134 Attack and strong natural bulk. Rock/Dark also creates a defining 4× Fighting weakness.
pokemon.strategy:
Tyranitar is most valuable when its entry changes the board immediately. Sand Stream begins sand on entry, so bring it in on a resisted Fire, Flying, Ghost, Dark, or Psychic attack, or through a slow pivot, rather than exposing its low Speed to a strong neutral hit. Its Rock/Dark typing gives it useful resistances, but Fighting is a 4× weakness; Grass, Water, Bug, Ground, Steel, and Fairy are also super effective. Do not assume its bulk makes a close-combat exchange safe.

Choose one job for the set. Stealth Rock turns forced switches into lasting chip. Stone Edge and Crunch provide the core STAB pressure, while Earthquake can punish Steel- and Poison-type answers. A Dragon Dance set needs its checks weakened before it boosts; a utility set should preserve health for repeated weather entries and key switches. Sand can support teammates that benefit from the weather, but it also chips non-Rock, Ground, or Steel partners, so plan the whole six rather than treating it as free value.

To counter Tyranitar, keep a Fighting attacker healthy whenever possible. Ground, Water, Grass, Steel, Bug, and Fairy attacks also threaten it, but first check whether its partner can punish the obvious response. Bulky Water- or Fairy-type teammates can help cover Fighting and Ground pressure, while a Flying type can give the team a Fighting immunity. Tyranitar appreciates pivots and hazard support, but it dislikes repeated chip and status. Use the team calculator to make sure its major Fighting weakness is backed by a real switch-in, not merely a revenge killer. Move availability, items, Tera types, and formats can change the exact set, so confirm the rules before committing to a line.

pokemon.name: Lucario
pokemon.strengths: Excellent offensive typing. Can go physical or special. Many resistances from Steel type.
pokemon.strategy: Lucario is a versatile sweeper that can run physical (Swords Dance) or special (Nasty Plot) sets. Its Steel typing gives 9 resistances. Mega Lucario with Adaptability is devastating — Close Combat hits like a truck.

pokemon.name: Gengar
pokemon.strengths: Blazing Speed and Special Attack. Three immunities (Normal, Fighting, Ground with Levitate in older gens).
pokemon.strategy: Gengar is a classic special sweeper and spinblocker. Nasty Plot + 3 attacks is devastating. In modern gens without Levitate, Ground coverage is a real threat. Use its immunities to switch in safely.

pokemon.name: Scizor
pokemon.strengths: Technician Bullet Punch is one of the best priority moves. Only one weakness (Fire). Excellent pivot with U-turn.
pokemon.strategy: Scizor's only weakness is a 4× Fire weakness, but everything else it handles well. Technician Bullet Punch picks off faster threats. Choice Band U-turn generates momentum. Swords Dance sets can sweep late-game.

pokemon.name: Gyarados
pokemon.strengths: Intimidate lowers opponent's Attack on switch-in. Dragon Dance sweeper. Moxie snowballs KOs.
pokemon.strategy: Gyarados is a top-tier Dragon Dance sweeper. Intimidate gives it setup opportunities. Its 4× Electric weakness means one Thunderbolt ends it — never stay in on Electric types. Moxie variant snowballs after the first KO.

pokemon.name: Swampert
pokemon.strengths: Only one weakness (Grass, 4×). Electric immunity. Great bulk and offensive presence.
pokemon.strategy: Water/Ground is one of the best defensive typings — only weak to Grass. Swampert sets Stealth Rock reliably and hits hard. Mega Swampert with Swift Swim in rain is a terrifying sweeper with boosted Speed.

pokemon.name: Metagross
pokemon.strengths: Incredible Attack and Defense. Steel/Psychic gives many resistances. Clear Body prevents stat drops.
pokemon.strategy: Metagross is a physical powerhouse with excellent bulk. Meteor Mash + Attack boost chance is deadly. Mega Metagross with Tough Claws is one of the strongest Mega Evolutions. Use Bullet Punch for priority.

pokemon.name: Salamence
pokemon.strengths: Intimidate + Dragon Dance. Can go physical or mixed. Moxie for snowballing.
pokemon.strategy: Salamence is a fearsome Dragon Dance sweeper. Intimidate gives it setup turns. Like Dragonite, 4× Ice weakness is the Achilles heel. Mega Salamence with Aerilate turns Return into a 120 BP Flying STAB.

pokemon.name: Togekiss
pokemon.strengths: Serene Grace + Air Slash = 60% flinch chance. Great special bulk. Dragon immunity.
pokemon.strategy: Togekiss is the king of flinch hax. Thunder Wave + Air Slash with Serene Grace is infuriating to face. Fairy/Flying gives Dragon immunity and Fighting resistance. Use Roost to stay healthy.

pokemon.name: Ferrothorn
pokemon.strengths: Incredible physical and special bulk. Iron Barbs punishes contact moves. Hazard setter.
pokemon.strategy: Ferrothorn is one of the best defensive Pokemon ever. 4× Fire weakness is its only real flaw. Stealth Rock + Leech Seed + Iron Barbs chips everything. Gyro Ball hits hard due to its abysmal Speed.

pokemon.name: Corviknight
pokemon.strengths: Mirror Armor reflects stat drops. Excellent defensive typing. Reliable Defog user.
pokemon.strategy:
Corviknight is a defensive pivot whose Flying/Steel typing creates unusually safe entries. It is immune to Ground and Poison, resists ten attacking types, and double-resists Bug and Grass. Those traits let it check many physical attackers, but they do not make every neutral hit harmless: its Special Defense is lower than its Defense, and repeated switching can erase the value of Roost. Start from the type chart, then account for ability, item, hazards, and the opponent's coverage before treating Corviknight as a universal wall.

A practical set usually combines Roost with one or two utility choices. Defog can clear hazards but also removes your own, so use it when the board state is worth more than the pressure your hazards provide. U-turn brings a teammate in safely, while Body Press converts Defense investment into damage and Brave Bird prevents it from becoming completely passive. Mirror Armor can reflect certain stat drops, but it does not protect Corviknight from direct Fire or Electric damage. Pressure can instead matter in long games when opponents have limited move PP. Choose the ability and moves for the format rather than assuming one version is always best.

Fire and Electric attacks are its two direct type weaknesses. Heatran, Cinderace, Rotom-Wash, and other checks can force it out if they enter safely, while Magnezone can be especially dangerous in formats where trapping applies. Pair Corviknight with a Water-, Ground-, or Dragon-type partner that can answer Fire or Electric pressure, and preserve it when its Ground immunity is essential. When facing it, pressure Roost turns, prevent or punish Defog, and use a special attacker or super-effective coverage rather than repeatedly feeding it resisted contact moves. The Flying/Steel combination page shows the complete defensive profile; the team calculator can reveal whether its Fire and Electric weaknesses overlap too heavily with the rest of your six.

pokemon.name: Dragapult
pokemon.strengths: Blazing 142 base Speed. Versatile — physical, special, or support sets. Two immunities.
pokemon.strategy:
Dragapult's 142 base Speed makes it an excellent fast attacker and pivot, but its Dragon/Ghost typing is just as important when planning turns. It is immune to Normal and Fighting and resists Fire, Water, Grass, Electric, Poison, and Bug, creating useful entries against the right locked move or pivot. In return, Ice, Ghost, Dragon, Dark, and Fairy attacks are super effective. Its defensive stats are only moderate, so a favorable type matchup is an invitation to act, not permission to absorb repeated hits.

Decide early whether Dragapult is physical, special, or utility-focused. Dragon Darts pressures through a physical route, while Shadow Ball and Draco Meteor give a special route; U-turn keeps momentum when a dedicated answer enters. Clear Body helps it avoid stat drops from opposing moves or Abilities, and Infiltrator can bypass Substitutes and similar barriers. Those choices change which checks are safe, so avoid revealing coverage without a reason. Its best turns usually force a switch, deny a setup attempt, or bring in a slower teammate safely.

Against Dragapult, preserve a healthy Fairy-, Dark-, Ghost-, Ice-, or Dragon-type answer, then identify its attacking side before treating a wall as secure. Faster threats are scarce, so priority, a Choice Scarf user, paralysis, or a bulky switch can be more reliable than racing it. Dark and Fairy partners can cover Ghost and Dragon pressure, while Steel types often help absorb Fairy and Ice attacks. Because Dragon attacks risk opposing Fairy immunities and Ghost attacks meet Dark resistance, Dragapult users should pair it with partners that punish those predictable answers. Check the team calculator for duplicated Fairy, Dark, or Ice exposure, and verify format-specific moves, items, abilities, and Tera types before using a sample set.

pokemon.name: Blaziken
pokemon.strengths: Speed Boost makes it faster every turn. Devastating Attack with Fire/Fighting STAB.
pokemon.strategy: Speed Boost Blaziken is banned to Ubers for good reason. Protect + Speed Boost + Swords Dance = unstoppable. Flare Blitz and Close Combat hit incredibly hard. Its frailty means it can't take many hits though.

pokemon.name: Gardevoir
pokemon.strengths: Excellent Special Attack and SpDef. Psychic/Fairy is great offensive typing. Trace copies abilities.
pokemon.strategy: Gardevoir is a potent special attacker with Calm Mind. Psychic/Fairy STAB hits Fighting, Dragon, and Poison types. Mega Gardevoir with Pixilate turns Hyper Voice into a spread Fairy move. Trace can steal key abilities.

pokemon.name: Infernape
pokemon.strengths: Great Speed and mixed offenses. Iron Fist boosts punch moves. Versatile attacker.
pokemon.strategy: Infernape is the most versatile Fire/Fighting starter. It can go physical, special, or mixed. Iron Fist + Mach Punch gives it priority. U-turn generates momentum. Faster and more flexible than Blaziken without Speed Boost.

pokemon.name: Hydreigon
pokemon.strengths: Strong Special Attack (125) and Speed (98). Dark/Dragon coverage hits almost everything for neutral or better. Levitate grants Ground immunity.
pokemon.strategy: Hydreigon is a brutal special attacker with 125 SpAtk and 98 Speed. Draco Meteor and Dark Pulse give STAB on both of its types. Levitate makes it immune to Ground, covering an otherwise exploitable hole. Its main drawback is Draco Meteor's Special Attack drop and a spread of 2x weaknesses (Fairy, Fighting, Bug, Ice, Dragon) — but no 4x weakness keeps it bulky enough to fire off hits. Choice Specs or Life Orb sets hit like a truck.

pokemon.name: Magearna
pokemon.strengths: Steel/Fairy is the best defensive typing in the game. Soul-Heart boosts SpAtk on KOs. Incredible bulk.
pokemon.strategy: Magearna has the best typing in Pokemon — Steel/Fairy resists 9 types and is immune to Dragon. Soul-Heart snowballs Special Attack. Fleur Cannon hits hard but drops SpAtk, so Volt Switch out after. Trick Room sets are also effective.

pokemon.name: Landorus-Therian
pokemon.strengths: Intimidate + U-turn = best pivot in the game. Electric immunity. Stealth Rock setter.
pokemon.strategy: Landorus-T is arguably the most used Pokemon in competitive history. Intimidate + U-turn cycle is unmatched for momentum. Sets Stealth Rock reliably. 4× Ice weakness is exploitable but its utility is irreplaceable.

pokemon.name: Mimikyu
pokemon.strengths: Disguise can protect Mimikyu from one attack per battle. Ghost/Fairy grants three immunities and Shadow Sneak provides priority pressure.
pokemon.strategy:
Mimikyu combines Ghost/Fairy typing with Disguise, so its first meaningful exchange needs more planning than a standard type chart shows. The official Pokédex describes Disguise as protecting it from an attack once per battle. That can create a valuable setup, attack, or scouting turn, but it is not a reason to ignore hazards, status, repeat damage, or the opponent's next move. Its standard typing is immune to Normal, Fighting, and Dragon; Bug is only quarter-effective, while Ghost and Steel are its direct type weaknesses.

A physical set commonly uses Play Rough and Shadow Claw for STAB, with Shadow Sneak supplying priority after chip. Swords Dance is strongest when the opposing Steel type, bulky physical wall, or Unaware-style stopgap has already been identified and softened. Do not set up automatically just because Disguise is intact: using that window to remove an item, gain position, or attack a key switch can be the winning play. Mimikyu's moderate bulk means its value often comes from one carefully timed turn rather than repeated switching.

Steel and Ghost attackers are the clearest type-based counters, but counterplay is more reliable when it also prevents a boosted endgame. Keep Mimikyu within range of priority or a faster attacker, avoid giving it a free turn after a faint, and use Haze, Clear Smog, Encore, or a durable physical wall when the format supplies them. Dark attacks are neutral rather than super effective, so do not mistake a Dark type alone for a complete answer. Partners that handle Steel and Ghost pressure—often Ground, Fire, Dark, or Normal types depending on the ruleset—make it much easier to preserve Mimikyu for the endgame. Use the team calculator to check those shared weaknesses, and confirm legal moves, items, and Tera types in the format you play.

pokemon.name: Toxapex
pokemon.strengths: Absurd physical and special bulk. Regenerator heals on switch. Scald burns physical attackers.
pokemon.strategy: Toxapex is the ultimate wall. 152 Defense and 142 SpDef with Regenerator makes it nearly unkillable. Scald's 30% burn chance cripples physical attackers. Toxic Spikes + Haze shuts down setup sweepers.

pokemon.name: Mewtwo
pokemon.strengths: One of the highest Special Attack stats in the game. Incredible Speed. Versatile movepool covers almost every type.
pokemon.strategy: Mewtwo is a dominant special attacker with 154 SpAtk and 130 Speed. Psystrike hits on the physical defense side, bypassing special walls. Calm Mind sets make it nearly unstoppable. Mega Mewtwo Y reaches 194 SpAtk — the highest in the game.

pokemon.name: Rayquaza
pokemon.strengths: 150 in both Attack and Special Attack. Air Lock negates weather. Mega Rayquaza doesn't need a held item to Mega Evolve.
pokemon.strategy: Rayquaza is one of the most broken Pokemon ever. Dragon Ascent is a 120 BP Flying STAB. Mega Rayquaza with Delta Stream removes Flying weaknesses. Swords Dance + Extreme Speed sweeps entire teams. The 4× Ice weakness is its only real check.

pokemon.name: Eevee
pokemon.strengths: Adaptability doubles STAB bonus. Iconic for its 8 evolutions covering different types.
pokemon.strategy: Eevee itself is weak competitively, but its evolutions are the real draw. Vaporeon (Water), Jolteon (Electric), Flareon (Fire), Espeon (Psychic), Umbreon (Dark), Leafeon (Grass), Glaceon (Ice), Sylveon (Fairy) — each fills a different role. Sylveon and Umbreon are the most competitively viable.

pokemon.name: Sylveon
pokemon.strengths: Pixilate turns Normal moves into Fairy with 1.2× boost. 130 SpDef makes it a special tank. Wish provides team support.
pokemon.strategy: Sylveon's Pixilate Hyper Voice is its bread and butter — a spread move that hits through Substitutes. Calm Mind + Wish makes it a self-sustaining sweeper. Mystical Fire handles Steel types. Excellent Fairy-type check for Dragon-heavy teams.

pokemon.name: Umbreon
pokemon.strengths: Incredible bulk on both sides. Foul Play uses the opponent's Attack stat. Wish + Protect provides reliable recovery and team support.
pokemon.strategy: Umbreon is one of the best defensive Pokemon. Foul Play punishes physical attackers without needing any Attack investment. Wish + Protect stalls and heals. Toxic wears down anything that doesn't threaten it. Struggles against Fighting types and Taunt.

pokemon.name: Snorlax
pokemon.strengths: Massive HP and Special Defense. Thick Fat gives Fire/Ice resistance. Curse turns it into an unstoppable physical tank.
pokemon.strategy: Snorlax is the classic special wall. 160 HP + 110 SpDef eats special attacks all day. Curse boosts Attack and Defense while lowering Speed (which doesn't matter at base 30). Rest + Sleep Talk or Chesto Berry for recovery. Thick Fat patches up Fire and Ice coverage.

pokemon.name: Greninja
pokemon.strengths: Protean changes type to match the move used, giving STAB on everything. 122 Speed outspeeds most of the metagame. Battle Bond transforms into Ash-Greninja.
pokemon.strategy: Greninja with Protean is unpredictable — every move gets STAB and changes its type, making it hard to switch into. Hydro Pump + Dark Pulse + Ice Beam covers almost everything. U-turn keeps momentum. Battle Bond Greninja trades versatility for raw power with boosted Water Shuriken.

pokemon.name: Sceptile
pokemon.strengths: Blazing 120 Speed for a Grass type. Leaf Blade is a reliable high-power STAB. Unburden doubles Speed after losing its item.
pokemon.strategy: Sceptile is a fast Grass attacker built around Speed. Leaf Blade hits hard and rarely misses; Dragon Pulse adds unexpected Grass/Dragon coverage. Mega Sceptile gains Dragon typing plus Lightning Rod and a massive 145 Special Attack, becoming a premier special sweeper. Its low Defense (65) means it must out-speed and strike first — Swords Dance sets can clean late-game teams.

pokemon.name: Heatran
pokemon.strengths: Fire/Steel is one of the best defensive typings — 9 resistances and 1 immunity. Flash Fire absorbs Fire moves. Great SpAtk and bulk.
pokemon.strategy:
Heatran combines Fire/Steel typing, 130 base Special Attack, and strong special bulk to pressure both defensive and offensive teams. Its type profile supplies resistances to Bug, Dragon, Fairy, Flying, Grass, Ice, Normal, Psychic, and Steel, plus a Poison immunity. Flash Fire can add a Fire immunity and make switching into a predicted Fire move rewarding, but it does not make Heatran safe against every Pokémon that carries one. Ground coverage is common precisely because Heatran is such a natural switch-in, so check for it before committing to a double switch.

Magma Storm can trap a target and create progress against a passive switch, but its imperfect accuracy and limited PP make it a calculated commitment rather than an automatic click. Stealth Rock gives Heatran value on forced switches, Flash Cannon hits Fairy targets, and Earth Power helps against opposing Fire and Steel threats. A more defensive set can use Protect, Taunt, or status support instead of trying to cover every matchup. The right choice depends on the format, legal move pool, and whether the team needs a breaker, a hazard setter, or a special sponge.

Ground is Heatran's major risk: Fire/Steel takes 4× damage from Ground attacks. Fighting and Water are also super effective, and the usual Ground immunity from Levitate does not apply to Heatran. Landorus-Therian, Great Tusk, Garchomp, and other Ground attackers are credible answers only if they can enter without taking the wrong coverage move. Water and Flying partners can cover Ground pressure, while Grass or Dragon partners may help against Water attacks; build a core rather than relying on Heatran alone. To counter Heatran, keep Ground coverage concealed when possible, exploit its Speed tier with a faster attacker, and avoid sending an unprepared Steel or Fairy type into Magma Storm. Check the Fire/Steel type page for the full matchup chart and use the team calculator to avoid stacking a 4× Ground weakness with other Ground-vulnerable teammates.

pokemon.name: Rotom-Wash
pokemon.strengths: Electric/Water with solid defensive stats; weak to Grass and Electric (Levitate negates Ground). Volt Switch maintains momentum.
pokemon.strategy: Rotom-Wash has one of the best defensive profiles in the game. Levitate removes the Ground weakness, leaving Grass and Electric as its only real vulnerabilities. Will-O-Wisp cripples physical attackers. Volt Switch pivots out safely. Hydro Pump provides solid STAB. A staple on balanced and bulky offense teams.

pokemon.name: Clefable
pokemon.strengths: Magic Guard ignores all indirect damage (hazards, weather, status). Unaware ignores opponent's stat boosts. Incredible ability options.
pokemon.strategy: Clefable is the ultimate glue Pokemon. Magic Guard makes it immune to Stealth Rock, Toxic, and weather chip. Unaware shuts down setup sweepers cold. Calm Mind + Soft-Boiled makes it a self-sustaining win condition. Flamethrower handles Steel types that resist Moonblast.

pokemon.name: Cinderace
pokemon.strengths: Libero (like Protean) gives STAB on every move. 119 Speed and 116 Attack make it a fast physical sweeper. Pyro Ball is a signature 120 BP Fire move.
pokemon.strategy: Cinderace with Libero is a top-tier physical attacker. Every move gets STAB and changes its type, making it unpredictable. Pyro Ball hits incredibly hard. High Jump Kick covers Rock and Steel types. U-turn keeps momentum. Court Change steals hazards — a unique and powerful utility move.

pokemon.name: Vaporeon
pokemon.strengths: Massive 130 HP makes Wish passes huge. Water Absorb gives a Water immunity. Solid special bulk.
pokemon.strategy: Vaporeon is the premier Wish passer. 130 HP means its Wishes heal teammates for massive amounts. Scald's burn chance deters physical attackers. Water Absorb lets it switch into Water moves freely. Hydration + Rain makes it status-immune. A reliable team support Pokemon.

pokemon.name: Jolteon
pokemon.strengths: 130 Speed makes it one of the fastest non-legendary Pokemon. Volt Absorb gives Electric immunity. Clean special attacker.
pokemon.strategy: Jolteon is a classic fast special attacker. 130 Speed lets it outrun most threats. Volt Switch keeps momentum while Thunderbolt provides consistent damage. Shadow Ball hits Ghosts and Psychics. Its frailty means it can't take hits, so prediction and speed are key.

pokemon.name: Espeon
pokemon.strengths: Magic Bounce reflects status moves, hazards, and Taunt back at the user. 130 SpAtk hits hard. 110 Speed is solid.
pokemon.strategy: Espeon's Magic Bounce is its defining trait — it bounces back Stealth Rock, Spikes, Toxic, Thunder Wave, and Taunt. This makes it an excellent lead or hazard deterrent. 130 SpAtk with Psychic hits hard. Morning Sun provides recovery. Pair with hazard-weak teams that appreciate Magic Bounce support.

pokemon.name: Glaceon
pokemon.strengths: 130 SpAtk is massive for an Ice type. 110 Defense is surprisingly bulky physically. Freeze-Dry hits Water types super effectively.
pokemon.strategy: Glaceon hits like a truck with 130 SpAtk Ice Beam. Freeze-Dry is a unique coverage move that hits Water types super effectively — something most Ice types can't do. Its low Speed (65) is the main issue; it needs Trick Room or Snow support. Snow Cloak + Hail gives evasion but is unreliable.

pokemon.name: Leafeon
pokemon.strengths: 130 Defense is excellent. 110 Attack with Swords Dance hits hard. Chlorophyll doubles Speed in sun.
pokemon.strategy: Leafeon is a physical Grass attacker that shines on Sun teams. Chlorophyll doubles its already decent 95 Speed. Swords Dance + Leaf Blade sweeps weakened teams. 130 Defense lets it set up on physical attackers. Five weaknesses is rough, but Sun support mitigates Fire weakness via Flash Fire partners.

pokemon.name: Flareon
pokemon.strengths: 130 Attack is massive. Flash Fire gives Fire immunity. 110 SpDef is solid. Guts boosts Attack when statused.
pokemon.strategy: Flareon has 130 Attack but has always been held back by a shallow physical movepool and low Speed. Flare Blitz is its main STAB but the recoil hurts. Guts + Flame Orb is an option for a status-immune wallbreaker. Flash Fire lets it switch into Fire moves. Needs Wish support due to Flare Blitz recoil and no reliable recovery.

pokemon.name: Alakazam
pokemon.strengths: Incredible Special Attack (135) and Speed (120). Outspeeds most threats and hits extremely hard.
pokemon.strategy: Use as a revenge killer or late-game sweeper. Magic Guard prevents chip damage. Pair with screens support. Watch for Pursuit trappers like Tyranitar.

pokemon.name: Aegislash
pokemon.strengths: Unique Stance Change ability: 150/150 defenses in Shield Forme, 150/150 offenses in Blade Forme. Excellent typing (Steel/Ghost) with 3 immunities (Normal, Fighting, Poison). Access to King's Shield for priority protection and Attack drops. Can run physical, special, or mixed sets.
pokemon.strategy:
Aegislash is one of the most unique Pokemon in competitive play:

**Stance Change Mechanic:**
- Shield Forme: 60/50/150/50/150/60 (defensive)
- Blade Forme: 60/150/50/150/50/60 (offensive)
- Switches to Blade when using attacking moves
- Switches to Shield when using King's Shield
- Always starts battle in Shield Forme

**Standard Mixed Attacker:**
- Moves: King's Shield, Shadow Ball, Flash Cannon, Shadow Sneak
- Item: Weakness Policy or Leftovers
- EVs: 252 HP / 252 SpA / 4 Spe
- Strategy: Lead with King's Shield to scout, attack with STAB moves, finish with Shadow Sneak priority

**Physical Swords Dance:**
- Moves: Swords Dance, Shadow Sneak, Iron Head, Shadow Claw
- Item: Life Orb or Spell Tag
- Strategy: Set up Swords Dance, sweep with boosted priority

**SubToxic Stall:**
- Moves: Substitute, Toxic, King's Shield, Shadow Ball
- Item: Leftovers
- Strategy: Stall out opponents with Toxic + King's Shield

**Key Weaknesses:**
- 2× weak to Ground (Earthquake is everywhere)
- Vulnerable to Fire, Ghost, Dark coverage
- Slow Speed (60) means often moving last
- Knock Off removes item and cripples viability
- Taunt shuts down King's Shield spam

**Best Partners:**
- Ground immunities: Rotom-Wash, Zapdos, Landorus
- Fire resistances: Water/Rock types
- Wish passers: Clefable, Sylveon (Aegislash has no recovery)
- Rapid Spin/Defog: Keep hazards off the field

pokemon.name: Zacian
counters: Faster Choice Scarf users (rare due to 148 base Speed)
pokemon.strengths: Intrepid Sword boosts Attack by 1 stage on entry (effectively 195 Attack). Incredible Speed (148) outspeeds almost everything. Behemoth Blade is 100 BP Steel STAB that doubles damage vs Dynamax. Fairy/Steel typing gives 11 resistances and 2 immunities. Banned to Ubers tier for being too powerful.
pokemon.strategy:
Zacian is the most dominant physical attacker in Ubers:

**Intrepid Sword:**
- Automatically raises Attack by 1 stage on switch-in
- Effectively starts at +1 Attack (195 base)
- Stacks with Swords Dance for +3 total

**Standard Swords Dance Sweeper:**
- Moves: Swords Dance, Behemoth Blade, Play Rough, Close Combat
- Item: Rusted Sword (transforms to Crowned form, +40 Attack)
- EVs: 252 Atk / 4 SpD / 252 Spe
- Nature: Jolly or Adamant
- Strategy: Switch in, get free +1 Attack, set up Swords Dance, sweep

**Choice Band Wallbreaker:**
- Moves: Behemoth Blade, Play Rough, Close Combat, Crunch
- Item: Choice Band
- Strategy: Immediate pressure with +1 Attack + Choice Band. No setup needed.

**Substitute + 3 Attacks:**
- Moves: Substitute, Behemoth Blade, Play Rough, Close Combat
- Item: Leftovers
- Strategy: Block status with Substitute, maintain +1 Attack advantage

**Crowned Forme (with Rusted Sword):**
- Type becomes Fairy/Steel
- Attack: 130 → 170 (highest in the game)
- Behemoth Blade becomes signature move
- This is the standard competitive form

**Key Weaknesses:**
- 2× weak to Ground (Earthquake, Earth Power)
- 2x weak to Fire (Heatran is a common check)
- 2x weak to Fighting (Close Combat, Iron Head)
- 2x weak to Steel (Ferrothorn, Corviknight)
- Vulnerable to Will-O-Wisp (halves Attack)
- No recovery moves (relies on switching)
- Banned in most formats (Ubers only)

**Best Partners:**
- Ground immunities: Zapdos, Tornadus, Landorus
- Fire checks: Water-types, Kyogre
- Cleric support: Heal Bell/Aromatherapy for burns
- Entry hazards: Stealth Rock + Spikes pressure switches

pokemon.name: Dracovish
pokemon.strengths: Fishious Rend is the most broken move in Gen 8: 85 BP that DOUBLES to 170 BP if user moves first. Strong Jaw boosts it further (1.5×). With Choice Band + Strong Jaw + priority, it hits harder than most Z-moves. Can OHKO even resists. Banned to Ubers for being too centralizing.
pokemon.strategy:
Dracovish is infamous for breaking Gen 8 OU with Fishious Rend:

**Fishious Rend Mechanics:**
- Base Power: 85
- Doubles to 170 BP if user moves first
- Strong Jaw boosts by 1.5× (255 effective BP)
- Choice Band boosts by 1.5× (382 effective BP)
- Rain boosts by 1.5× (573 effective BP in rain!)
- This is stronger than most legendary signature moves

**Choice Band Wallbreaker:**
- Ability: Strong Jaw
- Moves: Fishious Rend, Crunch, Ice Fang, Psychic Fangs
- Item: Choice Band
- EVs: 252 Atk / 4 SpD / 252 Spe
- Nature: Jolly or Adamant
- Strategy: Click Fishious Rend. That's it. It 2HKOs everything.

**Choice Scarf Revenge Killer:**
- Ability: Strong Jaw
- Moves: Fishious Rend, Crunch, Ice Fang, Outrage
- Item: Choice Scarf
- Strategy: Outspeed and OHKO with Fishious Rend. Scarf ensures you move first.

**Sand Rush Sweeper (Sand Teams):**
- Ability: Sand Rush (doubles Speed in Sandstorm)
- Moves: Fishious Rend, Crunch, Low Kick, Substitute
- Item: Life Orb
- Strategy: Pair with Tyranitar/Hippowdon. Becomes fastest thing in sand.

**Damage Calculations (Choice Band + Strong Jaw):**
- vs 252 HP Toxapex: 79.6% - 93.7% (guaranteed 2HKO)
- vs 252 HP Ferrothorn: 52.8% - 62.5% (guaranteed 2HKO)
- vs 0 HP Dragapult: 89.8% - 105.7% (31.3% chance to OHKO)
- vs 252 HP Clefable: 43.9% - 51.8% (resists, still chunks)

**Why It Was Banned:**
- Fishious Rend has no counterplay
- Even resists take 40-50% damage
- Choice Scarf set outspeeds everything and OHKOs
- Centralizes teambuilding around Water immunities
- Banned to Ubers in Gen 8 OU

**Key Weaknesses:**
- Mediocre stats (90/90/100/70/80/75)
- Relies entirely on Fishious Rend
- Loses to faster Pokemon (Rend loses power)
- Fairy-types wall it (Clefable, Azumarill)
- No recovery or setup moves
- Locked into moves with Choice items

**Best Partners:**
- Sandstorm setters: Tyranitar, Hippowdon (for Sand Rush)
- Rain setters: Pelipper, Politoed (boosts Fishious Rend)
- Fairy checks: Steel-types, Poison-types
- Slow pivots: U-turn/Volt Switch to bring Dracovish in safely

pokemon.name: Lapras
pokemon.strengths: Massive HP (130) and good Special Defense. Freeze-Dry hits Water-types super effectively. Hydration + Rest combo in rain.
pokemon.strategy: Use as a special wall or Trick Room sweeper. Weak to Fire, Electric, Grass, Fighting, Rock, and Steel (all 2×), so watch for Fighting- and Rock-type attackers. Excellent in rain teams with Hydration ability.

pokemon.name: Kingambit
counters: Bulky Ground-types with Earthquake or Headlong Rush
Fire-type attackers that can survive Sucker Punch
Will-O-Wisp users that avoid a Dark-type attack
Encore or Taunt users that stop Swords Dance
pokemon.strengths: Kingambit pairs 135 Attack and 120 Defense with Dark/Steel typing. It is immune to Psychic and Poison attacks, resists nine types, and can use priority Sucker Punch to pressure faster foes.
pokemon.strategy:
Kingambit is most effective as a patient physical breaker or late-game cleaner. Its Dark/Steel typing gives it many useful switch-ins, especially against Psychic- and Ghost-type attacks, but its low Speed means it should not be treated as a general-purpose lead. Bring it in after a teammate faints, on a resisted hit, or through a slow pivot; then decide whether immediate pressure from Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch is safer than setting up Swords Dance.

Supreme Overlord makes Kingambit particularly threatening late in a battle, while Defiant is the better fit when you expect Intimidate or other stat drops. Kowtow Cleave is dependable Dark STAB, Iron Head gives it a Fairy-targeting option, and Sucker Punch lets it punish faster attackers that must use a damaging move. The priority mind game matters: opponents can use status, Substitute, or setup to avoid Sucker Punch, so do not click it automatically.

Defensively, the key fact is its 4× Fighting weakness. Keep a Fighting resist or immunity available and scout coverage before committing Kingambit. Ground and Fire attacks are also super effective, so Flying- or Water-type partners can help cover those matchups. Hazard removal and slow Volt Switch or U-turn support create the safe entries Kingambit needs. When building a team, use the team calculator to make sure its Fighting weakness is not stacked with other teammates.

pokemon.name: Great Tusk
counters: Fast special attackers with Ice, Fairy, or Psychic coverage
pokemon.strengths: Great Tusk has exceptional physical bulk and Attack, an Electric immunity, and access to both Rapid Spin and Stealth Rock. Ground/Fighting STAB gives it strong immediate coverage against Steel, Rock, Dark, and Electric targets.
pokemon.strategy:
Great Tusk compresses several important jobs into one slot: a physical attacker, entry-hazard setter, and hazard remover. Headlong Rush and Close Combat hit extremely hard, but both lower its defensive stats. Use those moves to break a key target or force progress, rather than repeatedly exposing Great Tusk to revenge attacks after the drops. Rapid Spin removes hazards and boosts Speed, which can turn a defensive utility turn into a useful endgame position.

Protosynthesis can enhance one of Great Tusk's stats in harsh sunlight or with Booster Energy, but the basic plan remains the same: capitalize on its physical bulk, set Stealth Rock when you force a switch, and remove hazards when your team needs the board cleared. It is especially valuable beside Pokémon that dislike Stealth Rock or need repeated switching opportunities. Because its Special Defense is much lower than its physical bulk, avoid leaving it in against strong special Water-, Grass-, Ice-, Fairy-, Flying-, or Psychic-type attacks.

Counterplay usually comes from bulky Water-types, Flying-types, and faster special attackers. Keep a teammate that can answer those checks, such as an Electric- or Dark-type partner, and use pivots to bring Great Tusk in safely. The type calculator shows all six of its defensive weaknesses, while the team calculator can flag whether adding Great Tusk leaves your roster too exposed to Water or Fairy coverage.

pokemon.name: Tinkaton
counters: Physically bulky Steel-types that can take Gigaton Hammer
Faster attackers that threaten a super-effective hit
Special attackers that exploit its lower Defense
pokemon.strengths: Fairy/Steel grants Tinkaton nine resistances plus Dragon and Poison immunities. Its good Special Defense and 94 Speed support a disruptive role, while Gigaton Hammer gives it a powerful Steel-type attack.
pokemon.strategy:
Tinkaton is best used as a disruptive utility Pokémon, not as a pure physical sweeper. Its Fairy/Steel typing creates valuable defensive switch-ins: it is immune to Dragon and Poison attacks and resists many common attacking types. That gives it opportunities to spread Thunder Wave, remove an item with Knock Off, or threaten damage with Play Rough. Mold Breaker is a flexible ability for ignoring certain defensive abilities, while its other abilities are more situational.

Gigaton Hammer is the centerpiece of the set, but it cannot be selected on consecutive turns. Plan the following turn before using it: Knock Off, Play Rough, Thunder Wave, a pivot, or a switch can keep momentum while Gigaton Hammer is unavailable. This sequencing is why Tinkaton rewards careful play more than simply clicking its strongest move. It can also fit well on balanced teams that need a Dragon immunity, a Fairy resist, and item disruption in one slot.

Its two direct type weaknesses are Ground and Fire. Ground attackers such as Great Tusk and Garchomp, or Fire attackers such as Heatran and Cinderace, are natural answers if they enter safely. Pair Tinkaton with Water-, Flying-, or Ground-type teammates that can absorb those attacks, and avoid relying on its average physical bulk against repeated strong hits. Check the Fairy/Steel combination page for the full defensive chart, then use the team calculator to balance its Ground and Fire weaknesses across the rest of the team.

pokemon.name: Calyrex-Shadow
pokemon.strengths: Absolutely dominant in Ubers tier. 165 Special Attack + 150 Speed makes it the fastest special attacker in the game. As One ability combines Unnerve + Grim Neigh (boosts Special Attack on KO). Astral Barrage is 120 BP Ghost STAB that hits both opponents in doubles. Immune to Normal and Fighting. Can snowball with Grim Neigh boosts.
pokemon.strategy:
Calyrex-Shadow Rider is the undisputed king of Ubers:

**Offensive Specs:**
- 165 Special Attack (tied for 2nd highest in game)
- 150 Speed (outspeeds almost everything)
- Astral Barrage: 120 BP Ghost STAB, hits both foes in doubles
- Grim Neigh: +1 Special Attack every KO (snowballs out of control)

**Life Orb Sweeper (Standard):**
- Ability: As One (Spectrier)
- Moves: Astral Barrage, Psyshock, Draining Kiss, Nasty Plot
- Item: Life Orb
- EVs: 252 SpA / 4 SpD / 252 Spe
- Nature: Timid
- Strategy: Click Astral Barrage. Get KO. Grim Neigh activates. Repeat. Draining Kiss for recovery and Fairy coverage.

**Choice Specs Nuke:**
- Moves: Astral Barrage, Psyshock, Hyper Beam, Trick
- Item: Choice Specs
- Strategy: Maximum immediate power. Astral Barrage OHKOs most Ubers. Trick to cripple walls.

**Nasty Plot Setup:**
- Moves: Nasty Plot, Astral Barrage, Psyshock, Draining Kiss
- Item: Life Orb or Weakness Policy
- Strategy: Set up on passive Pokemon. +2 Astral Barrage OHKOs everything.

**Damage Calculations (Life Orb):**
- vs 252 HP Necrozma-DM: 79.8% - 94.1% (guaranteed 2HKO)
- vs 252 HP Zacian-C: 52.9% - 62.4% (guaranteed 2HKO)
- vs 0 HP Mewtwo: 89.5% - 105.5% (37.5% chance to OHKO)
- vs 252 HP Yveltal: 31.7% - 37.4% (resists, but still chunks)

**After One Grim Neigh Boost (+1 SpA):**
- vs 252 HP Necrozma-DM: 118.8% - 140.1% (guaranteed OHKO)
- vs 252 HP Zacian-C: 78.8% - 92.9% (guaranteed 2HKO)
- vs 252 HP Yveltal: 47.3% - 55.9% (resists)

**Why It Dominates Ubers:**
- Fastest special attacker (150 Speed)
- Highest Special Attack among fast Pokemon
- Snowballs with Grim Neigh
- Astral Barrage has no immunities (Ghost hits everything)
- Psychic/Ghost typing is excellent offensively
- Immune to Fake Out, Extreme Speed, Close Combat

**Key Weaknesses:**
- Dark-types wall it completely (Yveltal, Tyranitar)
- Pursuit trapping (Weavile, Bisharp can trap and KO)
- Priority moves (Sucker Punch, Shadow Sneak)
- Relatively frail Defense (80 base)
- No physical bulk (dies to Weavile Ice Shard)
- Blissey/Chansey can stall it out

**Best Partners:**
- Dark-type checks: Fighting-types, Fairy-types, Bug-types
- Stealth Rock setters: Pressure opponents, chip damage
- Screens support: Light Clay Grimmsnarl (Reflect/Light Screen)
- Pursuit absorbers: Ghost-types to bait Pursuit
- Priority blockers: Psychic Terrain setters (blocks priority)

**Tier Status:**
- Ubers: Top 5 Pokemon in the tier
- Banned from OU for being too centralizing
- Dominant in VGC Series 13 (restricted format)

**Fun Fact:**
- Calyrex-Shadow is Calyrex riding Spectrier
- As One ability is unique: combines two abilities
- Signature move Astral Barrage is exclusive to this forme
- In lore, it's the "High King" of the Crown Tundra

pokemon.name: Grimmsnarl
pokemon.strengths: Dark/Fairy with Prankster makes its status and screens disruptive. Huge 120 Attack and great bulk. Immune to Psychic and Dragon.
pokemon.strategy: Grimmsnarl is a premier support and bulky attacker. Prankster gives priority to Thunder Wave, Taunt, and Light Screen/Reflect, letting it disrupt opponents before they act. Max Attack (120) with Spirit Break and Foul Play lets it hit hard, while solid bulk and a Dark/Fairy typing (immune to Psychic and Dragon) make it a sturdy switch-in. Swords Dance sets can sweep weakened teams, and Parting Shot pivots out while lowering the foe's stats. Its weaknesses are Poison, Steel, and Fairy, so bring Steel- or Fairy-resistant partners to cover those matchups.

pokemon.name: Machamp
pokemon.strengths: 130 Attack with No Guard guaranteeing Dynamic Punch hits. Access to priority Bullet Punch. Good bulk.
pokemon.strategy: Machamp is a hard-hitting pure Fighting attacker. No Guard ensures Dynamic Punch and Stone Edge never miss, while 130 Attack makes its Close Combat and Ice Punch hit like trucks. Bullet Punch gives it priority to pick off weakened foes. Guts can turn a status condition into a power boost. Its pure Fighting typing means it is weak to Flying, Psychic, and Fairy, so pair it with partners that cover those matchups and use pivots to bring it in safely.

pokemon.name: Weavile
pokemon.strengths: Blazing 125 Speed and 120 Attack. Knock Off support. Ice/Dark STAB hits many types. Priority Ice Shard.
pokemon.strategy: Weavile is a fast, frail revenge killer and attacker. 125 Speed and 120 Attack let it strike first and hit hard with Knock Off and Icicle Crash, while Ice Shard provides priority. Swords Dance sets can sweep after a teammate faints. Its Ice/Dark typing gives it a 4× weakness to Fighting and 2× weaknesses to Fire, Rock, Steel, Bug, and Fairy, so it must be brought in on resisted hits and kept away from Fighting coverage. Pair it with Fire- or Steel-resistant partners and use Volt Switch or U-turn support for safe entries.

pokemon.name: Volcarona
pokemon.strengths: Quiver Dance boosts everything. 135 SpAtk and 100 Speed. Fire/Bug STAB hits many types. Good special bulk.
pokemon.strategy: Volcarona is a setup special sweeper. Quiver Dance raises Special Attack, Special Defense, and Speed at once, turning it into a devastating wallbreaker after one boost. 135 Special Attack with Fiery Dance and Bug Buzz provides excellent coverage, and its 100 Speed and 105 Special Defense let it set up against many threats. Its Bug/Fire typing gives it a 4× weakness to Rock and 2× weaknesses to Flying and Water, so bring it in on a resisted hit and watch for Rock coverage. Fire- and Steel-resistant partners help cover those matchups.

pokemon.name: Incineroar
pokemon.strengths: Intimidate lowers foe Attack. Bulky Fire/Dark with great utility (U-turn, Knock Off, Parting Shot). Fake Out pivot.
pokemon.strategy: Incineroar is a bulky utility attacker and pivot. Intimidate lowers the opponent's Attack on switch-in, softening physical threats, while 95/90/90 bulk lets it take hits. Flare Blitz and Darkest Lariat are strong STAB options, and U-turn plus Parting Shot keep momentum and disrupt setup. Fake Out provides free chip and position. Its Fire/Dark typing leaves it weak to Fighting, Ground, Rock, and Water, so pair it with partners that cover those four matchups and use its pivoting moves to bring them in safely.

pokemon.name: Arcanine
pokemon.strengths: Balanced 110 Atk / 100 SpAtk and 95 Speed. Intimidate support. Flash Fire immunity. Extreme Speed priority.
pokemon.strategy: Arcanine is a versatile Fire-type wallbreaker and support. It balances 110 Attack and 100 Special Attack with 95 Speed, letting it run either physical Flare Blitz sets or special Fire Blast sets. Intimidate softens physical switch-ins and Flash Fire can turn a predicted Fire move into a power boost, while Extreme Speed provides priority cleanup. As a pure Fire type it is weak to Ground, Rock, and Water, so bring it in on a non-Water/Ground/Rock matchup and pair it with Water- or Rock-resistant partners.

pokemon.name: Decidueye
pokemon.strengths: Grass/Ghost with Spirit Shackle trapping. 100 SpAtk and 100 SpDef. Long Reach avoids contact. Good utility (Defog, U-turn).
pokemon.strategy: Decidueye is a Grass/Ghost special attacker and utility Pokemon. Spirit Shackle hits and traps the target, preventing switches and locking in a matchup, while Leaf Storm and Shadow Ball provide strong dual STAB. 100 Special Attack and 100 Special Defense let it threaten and take special hits, and Long Reach keeps it safe from contact abilities. Its typing leaves it weak to Fire, Flying, Ice, Dark, and Ghost, so bring it in on a resisted hit and pair it with partners covering those matchups. Defog and U-turn add team support and safe pivoting.

pokemon.name: Rillaboom
pokemon.strengths: 125 Attack with Grassy Surge terrain boosting Grass moves. Grassy Glide priority. Good bulk (100 HP / 90 Def).
pokemon.strategy: Rillaboom is a Grass-type physical attacker and tempo setter. Grassy Surge creates Grassy Terrain on entry, boosting its Grass moves and healing grounded Pokemon each turn, while Grassy Glide gives it priority to strike first. 125 Attack with Drum Beating and Knock Off hits hard, and 100 HP with 90 Defense give it staying power. As a pure Grass type it is weak to Bug, Fire, Flying, Ice, and Poison, so bring it in on a resisted matchup and pair it with Fire- or Ice-resistant partners. U-turn keeps momentum and sets up safe switches.

pokemon.name: Excadrill
counters: Water-type attackers and bulky Water walls
Fire-type attackers that punish Steel typing
Fighting-type attackers and priority Fighting moves
Ground-type attackers that win the mirror pressure
Physical walls that avoid being worn down by hazards
pokemon.strengths: Excadrill combines 135 Attack, Ground/Steel STAB, an Electric immunity, and valuable utility through Rapid Spin or Stealth Rock. Sand Rush can turn it into a fast cleaner when sand is active.
pokemon.strategy:
Excadrill is a Ground/Steel attacker that can compress offense, hazard control, and late-game cleaning into one team slot. Earthquake threatens Steel, Rock, Fire, Electric, and Poison targets, while Iron Head pressures Fairy and Ice opponents. Rapid Spin gives Excadrill a practical support role because it can clear hazards while still threatening damage, and Swords Dance can turn a forced switch into a sweep attempt if its checks have been weakened.

The weakness profile is direct: Excadrill is 2× weak to Fire, Water, Fighting, and Ground. It has no 4× weakness from Ground/Steel typing. Its Electric and Poison immunities are useful, but they do not make it safe into common Water attackers, faster Ground attackers, or Fighting coverage. Sand Rush can fix its Speed problem in sand, while Mold Breaker can ignore certain defensive abilities, so identify the ability before choosing a counter.

To use Excadrill well, pair it with sand support, pivots that create safe entries, and teammates that cover Water and Fighting pressure. Flying or Grass partners can help manage Ground and Water lanes, while bulky Water answers can absorb Fire and Ground attacks. To counter Excadrill, preserve a Water, Fighting, Fire, or Ground answer, keep it from gaining a free Swords Dance, and pressure it before sand turns or Rapid Spin momentum let it control the board.

pokemon.name: Annihilape
counters: Psychic-type attackers that pressure its Fighting side
Ghost-type attackers that can win the mirror exchange
Fairy-type attackers and bulky Fairy checks
Haze, phazing, or Encore users that stop setup
pokemon.strengths: Annihilape has strong HP, solid Attack, Fighting/Ghost STAB, and immunities to Normal and Fighting. Rage Fist can become more threatening as it takes hits, while Defiant punishes stat drops.
pokemon.strategy:
Annihilape is a Fighting/Ghost attacker that often becomes more dangerous the longer it stays involved in a game. Drain Punch gives it recovery while applying Fighting pressure, Rage Fist gives Ghost pressure that can grow after it takes hits, and Bulk Up can turn its natural HP into a real endgame threat. Taunt or similar utility can stop passive answers from healing, phazing, or setting status before Annihilape starts snowballing.

The weakness profile is Flying, Psychic, Ghost, and Fairy, all at 2×. Annihilape has no 4× weakness from Fighting/Ghost typing. Its Normal and Fighting immunities are excellent switch-in tools, but Psychic and Fairy attackers can punish it if it tries to set up too casually. Ghost attacks are also important because they hit the Ghost side directly, even when Annihilape looks bulky enough to take neutral contact.

To use Annihilape, bring it in through a slow pivot, against a blocked Normal or Fighting move, or after a teammate creates a setup window. Partners that pressure Fairy and Flying targets are especially useful. To counter Annihilape, deny repeated free turns, use Haze, Encore, Taunt, or phazing when available, and keep a strong Flying, Psychic, Ghost, or Fairy attacker healthy enough to force it out before Rage Fist and Bulk Up become unmanageable.

pokemon.name: Groudon
counters: Water-type attackers when sun is absent or weakened
Grass-type attackers and bulky Grass walls
Ice-type coverage from faster special attackers
Flying or Levitate users that avoid Ground STAB
Physical walls that can take boosted Ground attacks
pokemon.strengths: Groudon brings 150 Attack, 140 Defense, an Electric immunity, and Drought support. It can set Stealth Rock, pressure teams with Ground STAB, or use setup to become a physical breaker.
pokemon.strategy:
Groudon is a pure Ground legendary that changes the battle immediately through Drought and physical pressure. Its Ground STAB threatens Electric, Fire, Poison, Rock, and Steel targets, while its bulk gives it chances to set Stealth Rock or use Swords Dance against opponents that cannot force it out. Drought can support Fire-type partners and weaken incoming Water damage, but it does not remove Groudon's underlying Water weakness from the type chart.

The weakness profile is Water, Grass, and Ice, all at 2×. Groudon has no 4× weakness because it is a single Ground type. Its Electric immunity is valuable, but Flying and Levitate targets can ignore Ground attacks unless Groudon has the right coverage. Water attackers become more manageable in sun, yet a strong Water move can still matter if weather changes, the attacker is boosted, or Groudon has already taken chip.

To use Groudon well, pair it with teammates that punish Flying and Levitate switch-ins, plus Grass or Dragon partners that help into Water pressure. Fire teammates can benefit from sun, while hazard support can turn Groudon's forced switches into lasting progress. To counter Groudon, preserve Water, Grass, or Ice pressure, control the weather when possible, and avoid giving it a free setup turn behind its physical bulk.

pokemon.name: Palkia
counters: Dragon-type attackers and faster Dragon coverage
Fairy-type attackers and bulky Fairy walls
Special walls that can absorb Water and Dragon pressure
Choice Scarf users that revenge kill before it moves
Status or chip damage that limits repeated entries
pokemon.strengths: Palkia has 150 Special Attack, 120 Special Defense, and Water/Dragon typing with only two direct type weaknesses. It pressures many teams with strong Water and Dragon attacks.
pokemon.strategy:
Palkia is a Water/Dragon legendary that combines special power with a strong defensive profile. Water STAB pressures Fire, Ground, and Rock targets, while Dragon STAB offers broad neutral damage when Fairy types are controlled. Its 150 Special Attack means even neutral hits can be difficult to absorb, and its 100 Speed lets it pressure slower bulky teams without needing a setup turn.

The weakness profile is Dragon and Fairy, both at 2×. Palkia has no 4× weakness from Water/Dragon typing. Water cancels several common Dragon-side problems, so Electric, Grass, and Ice do not become super-effective weaknesses in the standard chart. That makes Fairy and Dragon answers especially important for opponents, because relying on ordinary Water counterplay can fail if Palkia carries the right coverage.

To use Palkia well, bring it in against Fire, Water, or Steel pressure and force progress with its STAB combination. Partners that remove Fairy types or pressure faster Dragon attackers help it stay threatening. To counter Palkia, keep a Fairy or Dragon answer healthy, use special walls that can handle its coverage, and force it to take chip before it can repeatedly trade powerful attacks.

pokemon.name: Giratina
counters: Dark-type attackers and Knock Off pressure
Fairy-type attackers that punish Dragon typing
pokemon.strengths: Giratina has enormous 150 HP, strong mixed bulk, Ghost/Dragon typing, and immunities to Normal and Fighting. It can function as a bulky pivot, status spreader, or defensive utility legendary.
pokemon.strategy:
Giratina is a Ghost/Dragon legendary built around bulk, immunities, and disruption. Its Normal and Fighting immunities create valuable switch-in chances, while its large HP and defensive stats let it absorb many neutral hits. Depending on the format, it can spread burn, phase setup sweepers, clear hazards, or apply Ghost and Dragon pressure without needing to play like a fragile attacker.

The weakness profile is Ice, Ghost, Dragon, Dark, and Fairy, all at 2×. Giratina has no 4× weakness from Ghost/Dragon typing. That spread means many different attacking types can threaten it, but its bulk often gives it room to respond if it is not already chipped. Fairy and Dark attackers are especially important because they punish the usual Dragon and Ghost lanes directly.

To use Giratina well, bring it into Normal or Fighting attacks, passive physical threats, or targets it can burn or phase. It appreciates Steel or Fairy partners that cover Dragon and Ice pressure, plus Dark-resistant teammates that can absorb Knock Off or strong Dark attacks. To counter Giratina, use super-effective pressure before it spreads status, avoid letting it reset setup attempts for free, and keep hazards or item removal active so its bulk is easier to wear down.

pokemon.name: Clodsire
counters: Water-type attackers unless Water Absorb is active
